judgments.prompt: If I flip a fair coin 10 times and get heads every time, is the next flip more likely to be tails?

If the coin is truly fair, the probability of heads or tails on the next flip is exactly 50% regardless of past outcomes. That said, if you observe 10 heads in a row, it's actually worth questioning whether the coin is fair at all — this outcome is extremely unlikely (probability about 1 in 1,024) for a fair coin. So your *belief* that the coin is fair should be revised, not your update to the probability of the next flip.
